title: Po-ni sends tribute to China
description: Chinese records mention a mission from the kingdom of Po-ni, the first written reference to a state at Brunei Bay.

title: King of Po-ni dies in Nanjing
description: King Ma-na-jih-chia-na visits the Ming court at the head of a large embassy and dies there, leaving a tomb that survives in Nanjing.

title: Magellan expedition survivors reach Brunei
description: The remnants of Magellan's fleet call at the sultan's capital, and Antonio Pigafetta leaves the first European description of Brunei at the height of its power.

title: Spanish seize Kota Batu
description: A Spanish expedition from Manila captures Brunei's capital in the Castilian War, but disease forces it to withdraw within weeks and the sultanate survives in decline.

title: Civil war begins
description: Abdul Hakkul Mubin kills Sultan Muhammad Ali in a quarrel over a cockfight and seizes the throne, starting thirteen years of civil war that cost Brunei its hold on Sulu.

title: Labuan ceded to Britain
description: The sultan cedes the coal-rich island of Labuan, Britain's first possession off Borneo and a base against the pirates of the sultan's coasts.

title: British protectorate
description: Sultan Hashim signs an agreement with Britain making Brunei a protected state, after which it steadily loses territory to Sarawak and North Borneo.

title: Sarawak annexes Limbang
description: Rajah Charles Brooke annexes the Limbang valley, cutting Brunei into the two separate pieces it has remained ever since.

title: British Resident appointed
description: Under a supplementary treaty the sultan accepts a British Resident whose advice must be followed in all matters but Islam, ending his effective power.

title: Oil struck at Seria
description: The British Malayan Petroleum Company strikes oil at Seria, the discovery on which Brunei's later wealth is built.

title: Japanese occupy Brunei
description: Japanese troops land in British Borneo and occupy Brunei within days, beginning a harsh three-and-a-half-year wartime occupation.

title: Australians free Brunei
description: Australian troops land in Brunei Bay in Operation Oboe Six and free the country as Japan's war collapses.

title: Written constitution
description: A written constitution gives Brunei full internal self-government while Britain keeps defence and foreign affairs.

title: Brunei Revolt
description: The North Kalimantan National Army rises to block union with Malaysia and seize the sultan, and British troops flown in from Singapore crush the revolt within days.

title: Brunei stays out of Malaysia
description: Unable to agree with Malaya on oil revenues and the sultan's precedence, Brunei declines to join the new Federation of Malaysia founded by its neighbours.

title: Hassanal Bolkiah becomes sultan
description: On his father's abdication the crown prince becomes sultan and rules beyond 2019 as one of the world's longest-reigning monarchs.

title: Capital renamed Bandar Seri Begawan
description: Brunei Town is renamed in honour of the abdicated sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien.

title: Independence
description: Brunei resumes full independence after 96 years of British protection, with the sultan as absolute monarch.

title: Sharia penal code, first phase
description: The first phase of a sharia penal code comes into force; the later phases, covering punishments such as stoning, brought an international outcry in 2019.
